title: POC weekly sync - reliability incident follow-up
summary: Follow-up on last week's reliability incidents: intermittent 5xx and timeouts during peak test window. We reviewed logs, retry/backoff behavior, rate-limit responses, and quick mitigations (temporary rate-limit increase, client retries). Agreed to run an extended load test with tracing enabled, share debug logs, and instrument more granular SLO alerts. Next step: Redwood to provide adjusted rate-limit policy and debug bundle; Acme to run smoke test and confirm degraded-path behaviour in staging.
topics: Incident timeline; root-cause hypotheses (thundering herd on start, KV cache warm-up, upstream NLB 502s); retry/backoff tuning; rate-limiting and throttling behavior; observability gaps; next steps and ownership
next_steps: Redwood (Sara) will send debug log bundle and tracing instructions by 2026-05-01
Acme (Maya) will run extended load test in staging 2026-05-03 and share results
Redwood (Alex) to propose temporary rate-limit increase and retry/backoff config by 2026-05-01
Both teams to schedule a 30-min follow-up after tests (target week of 2026-05-04)
action_items: Owner: Sara Patel | Item: Export debug logs (ingestion, 5xx traces, request IDs) and upload to shared drive | Due: 2026-05-01
Owner: Alex Chen | Item: Draft recommended rate-limit + retry policy (incl. exponential backoff, jitter) | Due: 2026-05-01
Owner: Maya Lopez | Item: Execute extended load test (10k RPS simulated for 10 minutes) in staging and collect metrics | Due: 2026-05-03
Owner: Evan Brooks | Item: Run KV cache warm-up script and verify cache hit ratios before test | Due: 2026-05-02
transcript:
Header: 2026-04-29 15:00 UTC | Duration: 38 minutes | Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Sara Patel (Redwood SE), Tom Reynolds (Redwood CSM), Jared Kim (Acme CTO), Maya Lopez (Platform), Evan Brooks (ML)

[00:00] Alex Chen: All right, thanks everyone for joining. Quick agenda — incident follow-up, what we learned from the logs, tuning suggestions, and next steps. Maya, do you want to kick off with what you saw last week?
[00:18] Maya Lopez: Yeah thanks. So during our 9am load window on Thursday we saw a bunch of timeouts then about a 10-minute period with 5xxs, mostly 502s and a couple 504s. Latency spiked to 12s on some requests. We had client retries which amplified the traffic.
[00:36] Evan Brooks: To add, the error rate correlated with the first minute of the load ramp — looks like a thundering herd when new tokens and cold kv cache. We haven't warmed KV cache across pods so cold starts are likely.
[00:52] Sara Patel: Okay that matches what we saw from our traces. A few notes: there were upstream NLB 502s in the same window, and our proxy returned 429 for some bursts. The client library's retry was immediate retry x3 with no jitter — that tends to make spikes worse.
[01:15] Jared Kim: Is 429 coming from Redwood or our infra? We saw both 5xx and 429s.
[01:21] Sara Patel: The 429s were generated by our request quota — the edge rate limiter. The 5xx 502s appear upstream at the load balancer before the request hits the runtime in some traces.
[01:34] Alex Chen: So two buckets: client retry amplification + start/ramp behavior causing backend instability, and a portion of errors from upstream LB or infra. We'll want to tackle retries and also mitigate with temporary rate-limit bump during tests.
[01:48] Tom Reynolds: From a CS perspective we recommended a temporary rate-limit increase for the POC until we resolve the warm-up flow. We can lock it to Acme's staging IPs.
[02:02] Maya Lopez: That'd help. Also want to note we use SAML SSO and strict egress rules; during the incident we had some pod restarts while pulling KMS keys — could be unrelated but worth checking.
[02:19] Sara Patel: Noted — we'll check KMS interactions. For retries, recommended change: exponential backoff with jitter, initial delay 100ms, max retries 4, and client-side circuit breaker when 5xx > 5% over 1 min.
[02:36] Evan Brooks: Sounds fair. Can Redwood push a recommended code snippet for our client library? We use okhttp in the ML service and python requests in the frontend.
[02:46] Alex Chen: Yes, we'll attach snippets. Also we'll share a 'warm-up' script to prime KV cache across pods. That usually reduces cold-start 5xx.
[02:57] Maya Lopez: On observability, we saw request_id in some traces but it's not consistently propagated through our retry chain. Means it's hard to correlate client retry sequences.
[03:12] Sara Patel: We'll include guidance to ensure request_id header persists across retries — and include an option to echo the request_id in the response for easier mapping.
[03:24] Jared Kim: Were there any security implications? e.g. data leakage with retries?
[03:29] Tom Reynolds: No PII surfaced in logs we reviewed; our debug logs are scrubbed. We'll provide SOC2 documentation if you need it.
[03:38] Alex Chen: Let's walk through the runbook items we executed: increased client throttles temporarily, captured full debug trace for the 9:15am window, and enabled more verbose runtime logs. We also checked for queue depth spikes.
[03:55] Sara Patel: On the debug bundle — we'll share a link after redaction: https://redwood.example.com/poc/debug/acme-20260429 (note: placeholder). The bundle includes traces, request/response snippets, and NLB logs where available.
[04:12] Evan Brooks: Great. For the next test, we want to simulate 10k RPS for 10 minutes to validate stability. Can Redwood handle that on the dedicated POC pool?
[04:22] Alex Chen: We can provision a short-burst capacity; we'll coordinate schedule. Two points: 1) we recommend warming KV cache first and 2) run a gradual ramp to avoid hitting LB connection limits.
[04:37] Maya Lopez: How about adding circuit-breaker on client side? If backend returns 502 for > 10% for 30s, back off for 60s.
[04:46] Sara Patel: That is reasonable. We'll propose config values in the doc. We also have backends that return 502 when internal queue exceeds capacity — the longer-term fix is improving autoscaling config, but for POC we'll focus on retry/backoff + warmup.
[05:04] Jared Kim: Any estimates on how much temp rate-limit increase costs? We want to know budget impact.
[05:10] Alex Chen: For a short burst the cost delta should be minimal; we'll include a rough estimate in the note. Tom, can you flag finance?
[05:18] Tom Reynolds: Will do.
[05:20] Sara Patel: Observability gaps — we recommend adding a per-route latency SLO alert and a 5xx rate alert with per-cluster breakdown. Currently alerts are at top-level which hides per-route flaps.
[05:35] Evan Brooks: We'll add those. Also could you add a small snippet to log cache hit ratio to the response headers during staging testing? That would help.
[05:43] Sara Patel: Yes we can include X-Cache-Hit in staging.
[05:46] Alex Chen: Quick recap of owners and dates: Sara to send debug bundle + traces (by 2026-05-01), Alex to send rate-limit and retry policy (by 2026-05-01), Maya to run extended load test (by 2026-05-03), Evan to run warmup script (by 2026-05-02). We'll meet the week of 2026-05-04 for follow-up.
[06:10] Maya Lopez: One more question — should we push patch to client library now or after we run the test? We prefer to test with existing client first then roll the lib change so we have a baseline.
[06:21] Alex Chen: Makes sense to baseline first. We'll do two runs: baseline then with the retry/jitter patch.
[06:28] Jared Kim: Ok and on security docs you mentioned SOC2? We'll need those for procurement.
[06:33] Tom Reynolds: I'll upload the SOC2 and ISO docs into the shared folder after call.
[06:40] Evan Brooks: Anything else on the error taxonomy? I can produce a short CSV mapping request_id, timestamp, status for the incident window and attach to the load test results.
[06:50] Sara Patel: Please do — that will help correlate.
[06:56] Alex Chen: All right thanks everyone. I'll send meeting notes and the config proposals.
[07:02] Jared Kim: Thanks.

Notes: transcription contains minor mis-hearings (e.g., KV cache sometimes transcribed as keyv cache, VPC as VPN in one trace). Links and doc names are placeholders.
